content.short: M0 is a decentralized coordination layer for institutionally issued, RWA-backed stablecoins.
content.description: M0 is an institutional-grade decentralized protocol that serves as a coordination layer for the issuance of $M, a high-quality stablecoin backed by Real-World Assets (RWAs) like U.S. Treasuries. Rather than being a monolithic stablecoin issuer, M0 provides a platform that allows vetted institutions to mint their own branded, yield-bearing stablecoins using M0's underlying liquidity and security framework. This approach enables a more distributed and transparent stablecoin ecosystem that bridges the gap between traditional finance and DeFi.

resources.title: A Brief Perspective on Money Technology
resources.tldr: Twenty years of finding the financial stack badly built, then encountering Bitcoin in 2012 and reading it as a candidate protocol for money rather than as an asset.

resources.title: Introducing the Two Token Governor
resources.tldr: Smart contracts were meant to remove trusted intermediaries, and governance quietly reintroduced them. Splits governance across two tokens so risk-bearing and steering need not be the same party.

resources.title: Expanding Available Collateral Structures for Minters
resources.tldr: Governance proposals to let Minters use additional structuring and asset management solutions for eligible collateral, with the Foundation giving non-binding opinions. Stablecoins framed as transparent balance sheets.
